# `js/no-unused-iterator-helper`

**No lazy iterator helper whose result is thrown away**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/strict` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (`.forEach()` runs the callback now and reads the iterator, which the lazy call never did; the author accepts that) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-unicorn/no-unused-iterator-helper` |

## What it checks

`.map()`, `.filter()`, `.flatMap()`, `.take()` and `.drop()` on an iterator return another iterator and read nothing until it is read. A call whose result is discarded — as a statement, under `void`, under `await`, in a `for` initializer or update — never runs its callback. The receiver must be known to be an iterator: `.values()`, `.keys()`, `.entries()` or `.matchAll()`, an `Iterator.from/concat/zip` call, a helper chain on one, a call of a local synchronous generator, or a plain `const` of one. A discarded `.map(callback)` gets the suggestion `.forEach(callback)` (one argument, no type arguments, no TypeScript assertion around it). A receiver from a call the engine cannot see, an object method or an async generator is not known and is not reported.

**Why:** An iterator helper is a recipe, not an action: dropping its result drops the work, and the code reads as if it had run.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/strict` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/strict"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/no-unused-iterator-helper" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/no-unused-iterator-helper" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/no-unused-iterator-helper" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/no-unused-iterator-helper" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/no-unused-iterator-helper" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/no-unused-iterator-helper": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/no-unused-iterator-helper: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/no-unused-iterator-helper expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/no-unused-iterator-helper --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/no-unused-iterator-helper       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/no-unused-iterator-helper  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
items.values().map(save);
```

#### Do

```js
for (const item of items.values()) {
  save(item);
}
```

#### Fixed

```js
items.values().forEach(save);
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
items.values().map(save);
```

#### Do

```jsx
for (const item of items.values()) {
  save(item);
}
```

#### Fixed

```jsx
items.values().forEach(save);
```

```

#### Do

  save(item);

#### Do

```
